page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-144 is a high-capacity instance featuring 144 dedicated vCPUs and 540 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server utilizes 72 physical cores with 2 threads per core running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor features a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-144 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, scoring 156268.58 on stress-ng multi-core tests and 135068.95 on the PassMark CPU suite. Memory performance is highly competitive, with read-only cached small-block bandwidth reaching 11548.62 GB/sec and large-block uncached write bandwidth at 213.92 GB/sec. The instance excels in specialized compute workloads, achieving top-tier results in software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. It also showcases strong capabilities in LLM inference, processing 322.88 tokens/sec for medium (7B) model prompts and 45.11 tokens/sec for large (70B) model prompts. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench text processing scoring in the average tier.

Given its high resource density and lack of local storage or GPU hardware, the c4-standard-144 offers a specialized cost-efficiency profile tailored for massive, CPU-bound parallel processing. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale block storage independently. This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as large-scale software compilation, multi-threaded data decompression, static web serving at scale, database operations, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
